## 1. One-paragraph verdict
Genuine VP9 bitstream (ffmpeg testsrc2-generated content, per name and clean decode). `file`: "Duck IVF video file, codec VP90, 320x240, 125 frames". My struct walk: DKIF, version 0, hdrlen 32, fourcc VP90, 320x240, rate 25/scale 1, header count 125 == 125 walked frames, zero truncation, zero trailing bytes, timestamps 0..124 strictly monotonic, first packet 7258 bytes. The independent ffmpeg 7.1.5 `libvpx-vp9` oracle decodes it cleanly; the yuv420p dump MD5 equals the pinned constant in vp9_differential.rs:70, so the pinned truth is reproducible outside the code under test.

## 2. What actually works (verified)
- python3 struct walk -> 125/125 frames intact, ts 0..124 monotonic.
- `ffmpeg -c:v libvpx-vp9 ... -pix_fmt yuv420p - | md5sum` -> `7b5cbbc70b04132c8c74fcd07576fd48` == pinned `yuv_md5` at vp9_differential.rs:70 (sed-verified).
- `ffprobe -count_packets` -> codec_name=vp9, 320x240, nb_read_packets=125 == lane's `frames: 125`.
- Baseline: cargo-test-workspace.txt:1384-1393 `differential_lanes_vs_ffmpeg_libvpx_vp9 ... ok` (suite 4/4) — this fixture was decoded through the wired path at baseline.
